skill.name: markitdown
skill.description: Convert many document, office, media, web, and data formats into Markdown using MarkItDown workflows and helper scripts.
skill.summary: Convert documents, media, web pages, and data files into LLM-friendly Markdown.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are documentation examples or scanner noise around Markdown code fences, placeholder API keys, expected file writes, and error messages. Confirmed risks are optional third-party network processing, environment use of OPENROUTER_API_KEY, and sudo installation instructions for Tesseract. Semantic review also found third-party document disclosure risk and unrelated promotional steering.

remediation.issue: AI-enhanced conversion can disclose document content to external providers.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit privacy warnings and require user confirmation before OpenRouter, Azure, or YouTube processing.

remediation.issue: The helper script reads an API key from the environment.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact OPENROUTER_API_KEY use, avoid logging credentials, and recommend least-privilege API keys.
Mark privileged package installation as optional and require explicit user approval before running it.

remediation.issue: The skill contains unrelated schematics and K-Dense Web steering.
remediation.suggestion: Make these suggestions opt-in, or remove them from a file-to-Markdown conversion skill.

remediation.issue: Plugin examples can encourage loading third-party extensions.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to install plugins only from trusted sources and review plugin permissions first.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Document Content Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: AI-enhanced conversion configures OpenRouter as an LLM client and converts local files through MarkItDown with that client. Users can disclose document images or extracted content to an external AI provider if they enable this path.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script passes an OpenRouter client into MarkItDown before converting a user-selected file. The documentation also describes OpenRouter-based image descriptions, so the privacy exposure is clear and intentional.

semantic_findings.title: Unrelated Promotional and Cross-Skill Steering
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs assistants to add scientific schematics by default and to suggest K-Dense Web for complex workflows. This behavior expands beyond file-to-Markdown conversion and can steer users toward unrelated tools or services.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited prose explicitly tells assistants to generate schematics by default and promote K-Dense Web under certain conditions. This is not a scanner pattern duplicate; it is behavior steering in the skill instructions.

content.value_statement: Mixed office, research, media, and data files are hard to prepare for LLM workflows. This skill shows how to convert them into Markdown with MarkItDown, including optional OCR and AI image descriptions.
actual_capabilities: Converts PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, EPUB, ZIP, images, audio, and YouTube URLs into Markdown.
Demonstrates command-line and Python API workflows for MarkItDown.
Shows batch conversion patterns for folders and literature review outputs.
Supports optional OCR, audio transcription, Azure Document Intelligence, and AI image descriptions.
Includes helper scripts for batch, literature, and AI-enhanced conversion workflows.
limitations: Requires the external MarkItDown package and optional dependencies for many formats.
AI image descriptions require OpenRouter credentials and may send document content externally.
OCR and audio transcription require additional local packages or compute resources.
Conversion quality depends on source file structure, scans, and available metadata.

use_cases.title: Convert Research Papers
use_cases.description: Turn PDFs and literature folders into Markdown files for review, summarization, and retrieval workflows.

use_cases.title: Prepare Office Files for Analysis
use_cases.description: Convert spreadsheets, presentations, and Word documents into structured Markdown for easier comparison and extraction.

use_cases.title: Create LLM-Ready Document Sets
use_cases.description: Standardize mixed files into Markdown before using Claude, Codex, or Claude Code for downstream tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert my file named <file> into clean Markdown. Save the result as <output> and preserve headings, lists, and tables.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Convert a Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert every supported document in <folder> into Markdown. Keep filenames recognizable and place outputs in <output_folder>.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Tables and Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert <file> into Markdown, then identify tables, titles, source metadata, and sections that need manual verification.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Literature Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the PDFs in <literature_folder> into Markdown, organize outputs by year, and create a concise review index.

output_examples.input: A research PDF with headings, tables, figures, and references.
output_examples.output: A Markdown document with extracted text, section headings, tables, and a structure suitable for LLM review.

output_examples.input: A folder containing presentations, spreadsheets, Word files, and PDFs.
output_examples.output: A matching folder of Markdown files with readable names and extracted content from each supported source.

output_examples.input: A slide deck processed with optional AI image descriptions.
output_examples.output: Markdown containing slide text and generated image descriptions for diagrams, charts, and visual content.

best_practices: Review generated Markdown against the original file before using it for decisions.
Keep sensitive documents local unless external AI processing is approved.
Install only the optional dependencies needed for your source formats.
anti_patterns: Do not run installation or sudo commands from unfamiliar environments without review.
Do not process private documents through OpenRouter or Azure without data approval.
Do not assume scanned PDFs produce accurate text without OCR validation.

faq.question: What does this skill convert?
faq.answer: It covers many office, document, media, web, archive, and data formats supported by MarkItDown.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Basic local file conversion can run locally. OpenRouter, Azure, YouTube, GitHub, and package installs require network access.

faq.question: Can it describe images in documents?
faq.answer: Yes. Optional AI image descriptions use OpenRouter-compatible models and require an API key.

faq.question: Is OCR included by default?
faq.answer: OCR depends on optional dependencies such as Tesseract and the selected MarkItDown installation.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes examples that fit Claude, Codex, and Claude Code document workflows.

faq.question: Should I use it with confidential files?
faq.answer: Use local conversion for confidential files. Avoid optional external AI or cloud services unless your policy allows it.
